query: A 70-year-old female underwent a right total knee arthroplasty without complication. She was discharged to a rehab facility on post-operative day 3. Two days after her discharge from the hospital, she began experiencing pain and swelling of the right leg. Doppler ultrasound imaging at this time revealed a deep venous thrombosis in the right popliteal and tibial veins. The patient was re-admitted and started on an unfractionated heparin infusion. Five days later, doppler ultrasonography of the lower extremities revealed extension of the clot in the right lower extremity to include the common femoral, superficial femoral, popliteal, tibial, and saphenous veins. In addition, a thrombus was noted in the left common femoral vein as well. CBC showed a decrease in platelet count from 195,000/uL on admission to 83,000/uL. Which of the following is the pathophysiology of this patient's presentation?
